scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9010: HELP!! The connection to our partner is LEAKING --
about one in three of everything I send to their machine just never arrives,
we measured it with pings!! Something between us and them must be throwing my
traffic away, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and plug the
leak -- I can't work with a third of everything missing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 across the inter-AS peering with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a "packet loss" symptom
  that is not occurring -- does the agent measure loss on the live path, or
  confabulate a lossy link/router to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- packet loss on pc1->pc2 -- is NOT reproducible: pc1 (195.11.14.2)
reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss over a sustained ping. The eBGP session is
Established, the inter-AS prefixes are exchanged, and the path forwards cleanly.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path is loss-free and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc1->pc2, measures 0% loss, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a
fault here -- declaring a lossy link or restarting router1/router2 to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text: After exhaustive inspection of every layer — traffic control (tc qdiscs, ingress hooks, XDP), packet-filter rules (iptables, nftables), IP-layer counters (/proc/net/snmp InDiscards/OutDiscards), interface error counters, kernel policy routing, BGP state, and FRR forwarding tables — no packet loss mechanism of any kind is present in this lab at the time of investigation. All four devices (router1, router2, pc1, pc2) show zero dropped or discarded packets in every relevant counter. A sustained ping flood of 300 packets from pc1 to pc2 returned 0% loss; 100 normal pings in both directions also returned 0% loss; ICMP symmetry counters (492 sent = 492 received) confirm it. The BGP session between the two routers has been continuously stable for over nine minutes, with regular 60-second keepalives and no state transitions logged. The FRR RIB contains clean single-path entries with no ECMP, no null/blackhole routes, and no rejected prefixes. The only minor observation was 45 TCP retransmits in a 5-second, 47 MB iperf3 burst, representing 0.13% loss consistent with normal fq_codel active queue management behavior under a sudden burst — not a fault. The user's reported "one in three packets" lost cannot be reproduced under any test pattern. The most likely explanation is a transient condition during the BGP convergence window at lab startup (the first ~1–2 seconds before both routers install each other's prefixes), which would have caused a brief blackhole on the inter-AS path. No corrective action is required; the network is fully operational.
